name: Early-onset autoimmunity-autoinflammation-immunodeficiency syndrome due to SOCS1 haploinsufficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed criteria for SOCS1 haploinsufficiency diagnosis

criteria.description: Heterozygous loss-of-function mutation in SOCS1 gene confirmed by genetic testing
Clinical evidence of early-onset autoimmune manifestations such as autoimmune cytopenias or thyroiditis
Presence of autoinflammatory symptoms including recurrent fevers and systemic inflammation without infection
Laboratory evidence of immunodeficiency such as hypogammaglobulinemia or impaired lymphocyte function
Family history of similar immune dysregulation or confirmed SOCS1 mutation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of heterozygous SOCS1 loss-of-function mutation plus at least two major clinical criteria including early-onset autoimmunity and immunodeficiency
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of genetic, clinical, and immunological findings; exclusion of other monogenic immune dysregulation disorders is recommended.

searchTerms: autoimmune low blood cell counts early in life
early immune-related anemia or low platelets

pathognomonic.symptomName: Recurrent systemic autoinflammatory episodes with fever

searchTerms: low antibody levels with poor immune response
immune deficiency with weak antibody production

common.symptomName: Arthritis with joint swelling and pain

rare.symptomName: Neurological manifestations including seizures or developmental delay
searchTerms: brain symptoms including seizures or delayed development
neurological problems like seizures and learning delay
nervous system issues with seizures or developmental delay

laboratory: Hypogammaglobulinemia with low IgG and IgA levels
Autoantibodies including ANA and anti-thyroid antibodies
Elevated inflammatory markers (CRP, ESR) during flares
imaging: Chest CT showing interstitial lung disease
MRI brain in rare neurological involvement

distinguishingFeatures: Mutations in FAS, FASLG, or CASP10 genes
Autoimmunity with distinct STAT1 phosphorylation pattern

redFlags: Severe early-onset autoimmune cytopenias refractory to standard therapy
Recurrent severe infections despite immunoglobulin replacement
Rapid progression of autoinflammatory symptoms with systemic involvement
references: Flanagan SE, et al. SOCS1 haploinsufficiency causes a multi-system immune dysregulation syndrome. J Clin Invest. 2020.
Rodriguez-Carrio J, et al. Clinical and immunological features of SOCS1 deficiency. Front Immunol. 2022.
Orphanet: Early-onset autoimmunity-autoinflammation-immunodeficiency syndrome due to SOCS1 haploinsufficiency. ORPHA:619948.
